data.heading: The boring but important bit.

Spark Life Electrical Contractors is a Registered Electrical Contractor in Victoria — REC 27391 — and carries full public liability insurance.

Every job we complete is wired to the AS/NZS 3000 wiring rules and issued with a Certificate of Electrical Safety. You get a copy; so does the electrical safety regulator. If any electrician can't produce a REC number and a certificate, that should end the conversation.

data.heading: 1970s board, brought up to date.
data.body:
A four-bedroom home still running ceramic fuses and one shared lighting circuit for the whole ground floor. We replaced the board entirely, split the circuits properly, and put RCDs on everything.

Half a day's work, power back on by mid-afternoon, and the owners finally have a board they can read.

data.heading: Whole-home LED changeover.
data.body:
Thirty-two halogen downlights swapped for dimmable LEDs across two storeys, with warm white through the living areas and a cooler neutral in the kitchen and laundry.

We replaced four old leading-edge dimmers at the same time, which is usually the reason people think LEDs flicker.

data.heading: EV charger, load managed.
data.body:
A 7kW wall charger into a garage on a board that was already close to full. Rather than a full upgrade we fitted load management, so the charger eases off when the oven and ducted heating are both running.

Cable run concealed the length of the garage, app configured for off-peak charging, done in a day.

data.title: Privacy Policy

data.content:
This policy explains what personal information Spark Life Electrical Contractors collects, why we collect it, and what we do with it. It is written to meet our obligations under the Australian Privacy Principles.

What we collect

When you contact us — by phone, email or through a form on this site — we collect the details you give us: your name, phone number, email address, the address of the job, and whatever you tell us about the work you need done.

Why we collect it

Solely to quote and carry out the work you have asked about, to issue certificates and invoices, and to contact you about that job. We do not sell your information, and we do not share it with third parties for marketing.

Who we share it with

Only where it is necessary to do the work: for example, providing your details to a supplier arranging a warranty, or lodging a Certificate of Electrical Safety with the relevant regulator as the law requires.

How long we keep it

Job records and certificates are retained for as long as required by Victorian electrical safety and tax law. Enquiries that do not become jobs are deleted once they are no longer useful.

Cookies and analytics

This site may use cookies and analytics to understand how visitors use it. This data is aggregated and does not identify you personally. You can block cookies in your browser without losing access to any part of the site.

Access, correction and complaints

You can ask us what information we hold about you, ask us to correct it, or ask us to delete it where we are not legally required to keep it. Email hello@sparklife.com.au and we will respond within a reasonable time. If you are not satisfied with our response, you can contact the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner.

data.title: Terms of Service

data.content:
These terms apply to quotes issued and work carried out by Spark Life Electrical Contractors (REC 27391) unless we have agreed something different with you in writing.

Quotes

Quotes are fixed for the scope described and valid for 30 days. If we open up a wall or a switchboard and find something materially different from what was quoted, we will stop, explain it, and give you a revised price before continuing. You will never receive a variation you did not approve first.

Access and site conditions

We need safe access to the work area, the switchboard and any roof or subfloor space involved. Where access is blocked or unsafe on the day and we cannot proceed, a call-out charge may apply.

Workmanship warranty

Our workmanship is guaranteed. If something we installed or repaired is not right, tell us and we will return and make it right at no cost. Materials and appliances carry their manufacturer's warranty, which we will help you claim.

What is not covered

Pre-existing faults outside the quoted scope, damage caused by others after we leave, and failure of appliances we did not supply are not covered by our workmanship warranty.

Certificates

A Certificate of Electrical Safety is issued for all prescribed work and provided to you on completion. Keep it — your insurer may ask for it.

Payment

Payment is due on completion unless other terms have been agreed in writing. Larger jobs may be invoiced in stages, set out in the quote.

Cancellation

Let us know as early as you can. Cancellations with less than 24 hours' notice may attract a fee covering materials already ordered for your job.

Australian Consumer Law

Nothing in these terms excludes, restricts or modifies any guarantee, right or remedy you have under the Australian Consumer Law.

data.heading: Switchboard Upgrades
data.body:
If your board still has ceramic fuses and fuse wire, it was built for a house with a fridge, a kettle and a telly — not induction cooktops, ducted heating, a home office and a car on charge. Rewirable fuses protect the wiring. They do nothing to protect the person touching it.

A switchboard upgrade replaces those fuses with circuit breakers and RCDs (safety switches) that cut power in around 30 milliseconds when current starts flowing somewhere it shouldn't. We split your circuits sensibly, label everything clearly, and leave you with a board that has room for whatever you add next.

Most upgrades are a same-day job. We'll let you know beforehand roughly how long you'll be without power, and we work to keep the fridge and the wifi up as long as we can.

Smoke alarms expire. Every one of them has a manufacture date stamped on the back, and after ten years the sensor is no longer reliable — regardless of whether it still chirps when you press the button.

For a new system, we do the electrical side: the circuit, the isolator and the connection. We work alongside your plumber so it's one coordinated job rather than two trades blaming each other.

faqs.question: Is my hot water problem electrical or plumbing?
faqs.answer: If there's no hot water at all and no leak, it's usually electrical — element or thermostat. Leaks, pressure problems and valve failures are plumbing. We'll tell you honestly which one it is rather than charging you for a call-out to say 'not mine'.

faqs.question: Should I switch to off-peak hot water?
faqs.answer: If your system is on continuous supply and your household's usage is fairly predictable, off-peak usually cuts the running cost of the tank by about half. It's a straightforward changeover.

faqs.question: How long does a hot water element last?
faqs.answer: Typically eight to twelve years, less in hard water areas. If your system is over ten years old and the element has already failed once, replacing the whole unit is often better value than another repair.

A split system is only as good as its install. Undersize it and it runs flat out and never quite gets there; oversize it and it short-cycles, leaving the room cold and damp. We size to the room — glazing, orientation, insulation and ceiling height all count.

The electrical side matters just as much. Air conditioners need their own circuit with correctly rated protection; run one off a general power circuit and you'll be resetting the breaker every hot afternoon.

We handle supply and install, or install a unit you've already bought, and we'll site the outdoor unit somewhere that won't annoy you or the neighbours.

faqs.question: What size air conditioner do I need?
faqs.answer: As a rough guide, about 0.15kW per square metre for a well-insulated room — but glazing, west-facing walls and high ceilings change that a lot. We measure and size properly rather than guessing from floor area alone.

faqs.question: Do I need a dedicated circuit for a split system?
faqs.answer: Yes, for anything beyond the smallest units. Running one off a shared general power circuit is the most common reason a new air conditioner keeps tripping the board on hot days.

data.heading: Outdoor & Garden Lighting
data.body:
Outdoor lighting fails for one reason more than any other: fittings and connections that were never rated for the exposure they actually get. Salt air down here is unforgiving, and a fitting that's fine under a covered alfresco will corrode in eighteen months on an exposed fence line.

We spec IP-rated fittings to suit each position, run cable at proper depth in conduit, and use weatherproof connections rather than taping joints and hoping.

Zoning is where it gets good: path and step lighting on a timer, garden feature lighting on its own switch, sensor-driven security lighting at the entries. All of it dimmable and controllable if you want it.

faqs.question: Will outdoor lighting survive the salt air down here?
faqs.answer: If it's specified properly, yes. We use marine-grade or coastal-rated fittings anywhere within reach of salt spray. It costs a little more up front and saves replacing everything in two years.

faqs.question: Can outdoor lighting run on a timer?
faqs.answer: Yes — timers, photocells that switch at dusk, or app control. Most people end up with path lighting on dusk-to-late and feature lighting on a switch they use when they're outside.

faqs.question: Is low-voltage garden lighting better?
faqs.answer: For garden beds and path lighting it's often ideal — safer to work around and easier to extend later. For floodlighting and alfresco areas mains voltage usually makes more sense. We'll mix the two where it suits.

faqs.answer: Usually. Single-storey homes with roof access are straightforward. Double-storey takes more planning, and occasionally a small access hole that we make good afterwards. We'll walk the route with you first.

faqs.answer: Yes. We run power and HDMI inside the wall to a recessed outlet behind the screen, so there's nothing visible at all.
